3. In addition, Glenn and Edwardst have examined the mass
spectrometry of one type of structurally-related nicotinoids.
This paper presents an extension of that work to other compounds
structurally similar to nicotine.
The widespread occurrence of nicotine-like compounds in
nature, as well as a continuing interest in understanding the
nature of these types of compounds in tobacco and tobacco smoke
provides cause for the present study. Also, mechanisms developed
here may be important in the understanding of similar substituted
pyridine systems.
Glenn and Edwards have presented an excellent description of
the comparisons between 2-nicotine (Fig. 1, 1), 3-nicotine (Fig.
1, 2), and 4-nicotine (Fig. 1, 3).* Our intent is to further the
study of nicotine-like compounds by including data from the
fragmentation of the isonicotines, compounds 4, 5, and 6 in Fig.
